query: For the paper "Lancaster A at SemEval-2017 Task 5: Evaluation metrics matter: predicting sentiment from financial news headlines" (arXiv: 1705.00571), answer this question: Do they use external financial knowledge in their approach?

drafts:
No, they do not use external financial knowledge in their approach.

The paper describes solutions to SemEval Task 5 Track 2 that utilise only SVR and BLSTM approaches, and states that "our approaches acted as sentence level classifiers as they take no target company into consideration" [15]. Consistent with this, their error analysis found that the BLSTM systems "do not know which parts of the sentence are associated to the company the sentiment is with respect to" [14], and future work is proposed to incorporate aspect-specific information into an LSTM model [6] — indicating such company/aspect-specific knowledge was not used in the described systems.

The paper describes their solutions to SemEval Task 5 Track 2 as utilising only SVR and BLSTM approaches, and states that "our approaches acted as sentence level classifiers as they take no target company into consideration" [15]. Consistent with this, their error analysis of the top 50 MAE errors found that the BLSTM systems "do not know which parts of the sentence are associated to the company the sentiment is with respect to" [14]. The proposed future work to "implement aspect specific information into an LSTM model" further indicates that such company/aspect-specific knowledge was not used in the systems described in this paper [6].

We analysed the top 50 errors based on Mean Absolute Error (MAE) in the test dataset speciﬁ- cally to examine the number of sentences contain- ing more than one aspect. Our investigation shows that no one system is better at predicting the senti- ment of sentences that have more than one aspect (1) (i.e. company) within them. Within those top 50 errors we found that the BLSTM systems do not know which parts of the sentence are associated to the company the sentiment is with respect to.

6 Conclusion and Future Work In this short paper, we have described our imple- mented solutions to SemEval Task 5 track 2, util- ising both SVR and BLSTM approaches. Our re- sults show an improvement of around 5% when using LSTM models relative to SVR. We have shown that this task can be partially represented as an aspect based sentiment task on a domain spe- ciﬁc problem. In general, our approaches acted as sentence level classiﬁers as they take no target company into consideration.
